summary: Email canonicalization mismatch prevents internal notebook sign-in and access reconciliation
description:
Issue summary:
A Redwood engineer cannot access internal notebook workspaces after SSO sign-in. The Okta SAML assertion authenticates but the session is tied to a secondary internal identity that has no notebook role bindings.

Impact:
Single-user (internal) access loss to notebooks; blocks debugging and scheduled runs for the engineer. No widespread service degradation observed, but the identity inconsistency could affect other users after provisioning changes.

Environment:
prod-us-west - notebooks service behind identity-proxy with SCIM provisioning from Okta.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Sign in to console via Okta for user alice+infra@redwood.com (sign-in prints success).
2) Attempt to open Notebook -> redirect completes but authorization to workspace fails with 403.
3) Navigate to support tool and inspect user identities. Two internal identities present: alice@redwood.com (primary, no notebooks role) and alice+infra@redwood.com (has notebooks role but not linked to SSO session).

Observed behavior:
- SSO/SAML assertion NameID shows email alice@redwood.com (lowercased, plus-tag stripped) while Okta profile externalId still contains plus-tag form.
- SCIM events show a recent canonicalization change that normalized email by stripping "+" tags; reconciliation job did not merge the two identities.

Expected behavior:
SSO/SCIM canonicalization must be consistent such that SAML/NameID maps to the same internal identity that holds role bindings, or automatic reconciliation should merge duplicates and preserve bindings.

Logs / Relevant traces:
- SAML assertion (trace-id: saml-7a2b): Subject: "alice@redwood.com"
- SCIM provisioning log (trace-id: scim-21f8): PATCH /Users/1189 - changed email to "alice@redwood.com" from "alice+infra@redwood.com"
- Notebooks auth log (trace-id: nb-9c3e): authorization failed - no role binding found for session principal id 0x4e2b

Temporary workaround:
Manual reconciliation applied by identity team: merged the two internal identities and re-attached notebook roles to the canonical account. User was able to sign in and access notebooks after a forced logout/login.

2026-03-10 09:40 - Marcus Li: Assigned. Requested SCIM provisioning logs and SAML assertion from the user session.
2026-03-10 10:05 - SupportBot: Collected SAML and SCIM traces (saml-7a2b, scim-21f8) and attached to ticket.
2026-03-10 14:12 - Identity Team (Olivia Nguyen): Found a recent proxy rollout that strips plus-addressing. Reconcile job did not run due to rate-limit errors during that window.

investigation_notes: Checked Okta profile for alice+infra@redwood.com - externalId unchanged; SCIM patch later normalized email to alice@redwood.com.

Identity-proxy change on 2026-03-09 introduced email canonicalization (strip plus-addressing) to comply with downstream analytics. The change was rolled out without updating the reconciliation schedule.
Reconcile job (identity-service/reconciler) was rate-limited by Okta API throttling between 2026-03-09 22:00 and 2026-03-10 02:00 which left duplicates unresolved.
Notebooks service expects principal.email to match existing role bindings exactly; mismatch results in lookup miss and 403. Consider switching to principal.internal_id or adding alias lookup.
Potential edge-case: users who used plus-addressing historically may now have two entries if SCIM normalization runs after a user used Okta initial provisioning with plus-tag.
resolution: Applied manual merge of the duplicate identities for the affected user and re-attached notebook role bindings. Asked the reporter to sign out and sign in to pick up the corrected mapping; access confirmed. Rolled back the email canonicalization rule in identity-proxy for the next 24 hours while we prepare a controlled migration. Created a PR to add an alias lookup fallback in notebooks-service and to harden the reconciler with exponential backoff and Okta retry logic (see PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-service/pull/1524). Follow-ups: schedule a controlled canonicalization migration with a reconciliation run and add a post-migration audit to Confluence runbook.
follow_up_actions: Create migration playbook to normalize addresses and run reconciler with quotas (owner: Olivia Nguyen)
Implement alias lookup fallback in notebooks-service to avoid authorization misses during migration (owner: Marcus Li)
Add Okta rate-limit handling and retries to reconciler (owner: Identity Team)
Postmortem note and runbook addendum on Confluence - link added to ticket
